chunks: Therefore, choose from your affairs that which will establish your excuse and with which your argument will be proven. Take from the transient things of this world that which will remain for you, prepare for your journey, grasp the lightning of deliverance, and saddle the mounts of readiness.
ai.seo_question: How does one prepare for the journey of death according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this exegesis of Surah Al-Munafiqun, Imam Ali (AS) interprets the verse as a call to strategic spiritual preparation, urging believers to select deeds that substantiate their faith and justify their standing before God. He emphasizes the transient nature of worldly possessions versus the permanence of the hereafter, framing death as a journey for which one must equip themselves with enduring spiritual assets. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *tawassul* through righteous actions and the conscious transition from the temporal to the eternal.
